{"path":"DESIGN-SYSTEM.md","content":"# Design system: Godzilla 1.0.0 Godzilla is the design system for RIFT CMS documentation sites — born from the rift where molten content rises to the surface. Warm volcanic neutrals, magma-orange accents, and a dense, link-heavy, code-heavy layout language built for technical docs (Astro-style hub/detail pages, left navigation, API reference tables, and syntax-styled code blocks). Every page on this site is built from these components and tokens. Use them rather than writing custom markup or styling — hand-rolled equivalents break visual consistency and will not pick up future design-system changes. ## Components ### alert Callout box for notes, warnings, and danger/breaking-change notices inside docs content. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `variant` | string | `info` | One of info, success, warning, danger. | | `title` | string | `Note` | Callout heading. | | `body_html` | html | `This endpoint is deprecated in favor of ` | Callout body content, may include inline links. | **Usage:** variant must match one of the fixed CSS suffixes: info, success, warning, danger. Any other value falls back to the default neutral alert border. ### card Link tile used on hub pages to point at guides, API endpoints, SDKs, or concepts. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `href` | string | `/guides/building-your-first-pipeline` | Destination URL. | | `tag` | string | `Guide` | Short category label shown above the title. | | `title` | string | `Building your first pipeline` | Card title. | | `description` | string | `Learn how to assemble your first data pi` | One or two sentence summary. | **Usage:** Use one card component call per tile on hub/index pages such as Guides hub, API Reference hub, and SDKs hub. ### chip Small inline badge used for version tags and status labels (e.g. v2, Beta, Deprecated). | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `label` | string | `v2` | Chip text. | | `variant` | string | `primary` | One of primary, success, warning, danger, info, or omit for neutral. | **Usage:** variant maps directly to a fixed CSS class suffix; unknown values render as the neutral default chip style. ### code-block Syntax-styled code block with filename/language header and copy affordance, used throughout guides and API reference pages. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `filename` | string | `pipeline.config.json` | Optional filename or example label shown in the header. | | `language` | string | `json` | Language label shown top-right. | | `code` | html | `{ "pipeline": "ingest-orders" }` | The pre-formatted code content (already escaped/highlighted markup if needed). | **Usage:** code is inserted verbatim inside a pre/code block; Troubleshooting / FAQ

Common problems, and where in the docs to go for the full explanation.

My pipeline isn't processing events

Check the source connector's health field via the Connectors endpoint. A down connector stalls every pipeline that reads from it. If it's healthy, confirm the pipeline itself is active and not paused — see Scheduling & triggers.

Events keep failing and landing in the dead-letter queue

Walk through Handling errors & retries — it covers both diagnosing the failure and replaying events once fixed.

I'm not receiving webhook deliveries

Verify your endpoint returns a 2xx status and that you're checking X-Godzilla-Signature correctly — a rejected signature looks identical to a dropped delivery from the outside. Full details in the Webhooks endpoint reference.

I'm getting 429s

You've hit a rate limit. Read Quotas & billing to understand plan limits and what to do when you exceed them. Use the Retry-After header to know when to retry.

Migrating from v1?

A number of "it worked yesterday" reports trace back to v1's offset pagination or polling patterns carried over into v2 code. See the Migration guide.

Still stuck? Get in touch

Before reaching out, make sure you've checked the sections above — most common issues are covered there.

Contact channels

  • Technical support: support@godzilladocs.dev
  • Sales: sales@godzilladocs.dev
  • Security reports: security@godzilladocs.dev — see Security & compliance overview for our disclosure policy.
Response times

Standard-tier support responds within one business day. Include your workspace ID and, if relevant, a request_id from an error response.

input.content:
🌋 Godzilla Docs
  • Versions
  • Migration guide (v2 → v3)
  • Migration guide (v1 → v2)
  • Release notes archive

Migration guide (v2 → v3) Recommended

v3 ships with event retention configuration — a simple but powerful feature for compliance-driven pipelines. The migration is minimal: the endpoint remains backward-compatible, so you can upgrade at your own pace.

What's new in v3

v3 adds a single new optional parameter to pipeline creation and updates:

  • retention_days — Control how long events are kept in each pipeline (1–365 days, default: 30). Allows fine-grained control over data lifecycle and compliance obligations without blanket org-wide policies.

All other endpoints and parameters remain unchanged.

Update client code

When you upgrade to v3, change your base URL and optionally add retention_days to any pipeline creation requests:

diff diff 
- POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines
+ POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3/pipelines

  {
    "name": "ingest-orders",
    "source_connector_id": "conn_pg_orders",
    "destination_connector_id": "conn_snowflake_dw",
+   "retention_days": 90
  }

New compliance features

Per-pipeline retention policies let you handle mixed data classifications in a single workspace:

  • PII pipelines — Set retention_days: 7 to comply with short data minimization windows.
  • Analytics pipelines — Set retention_days: 365 for longer historical context.
  • Audit logs — Set retention_days: 30 to meet standard compliance standards.

v3 enforces retention at the pipeline level, so different data flows can have independent lifespans.

Migration timeline

v2 will continue to work until end-of-life. No breaking changes are planned in 2026. Start with v3 on new integrations; migrate existing ones at your convenience.

v3 is backward-compatible

Omitting retention_days defaults to 30 days, matching v2 behavior. You can upgrade your base URL immediately and add retention policies gradually.

Migration notes

  • Events created under v2 inherit the new retention period retroactively — existing pipelines updated to v3 will apply the new retention_days to all retained events.
  • SDK clients may cache the v2 base URL — clear any cached configuration and redeploy.
  • The retention_days limit is enforced at request time; validation happens server-side, so older SDKs will still send valid requests to v3.

Still stuck?

Common migration issues are covered in Troubleshooting / FAQ. Or contact support if you hit any blockers.
